statement: For a finite poset P, a deleted chain C={c_1<...<c_m}, and Q=P\C, every tau in L(Q) has exact multiplicity W_C(tau) equal to the number of weakly increasing slot vectors s with a_j(tau)<=s_j<=b_j(tau). Hence e(P)=sum_tau W_C(tau), and restriction of a uniform L(P) to Q is weighted by W_C, not uniform in general.
additional_result: Forward/backward corridor counts F_t(r),G_t(r) give H_t(r)=F_t(r)G_t(r), the exact number of full insertion vectors with s_t=r; summing H_t(r) above/below pos_tau(q) yields exact q--c_t pair-order numerators.
obstruction: A three-element example has induced weights 2 and 1. A width-two family has max_tau W/min_tau W=s+1, so a universal bounded-density transfer from the uniform deletion law cannot prove the parent target.
next_implication: Prove a weighted 1/3-2/3 balance theorem for the interval-corridor measures W_C, or exploit local adjacent-swap/total-positivity structure to force a balanced Q-Q or Q-C pair.
verification_scope: Written bijection proof plus deterministic standard-library regression script; the script checks 1024 generated five-point posets and pair-order counts. Computational checks are evidence, not the proof.
